item.title: At Frankfurt Book Fair, Chinese publishers offer gateway to get to know China
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
The presence of Chinese publishers at the world's largest book fair is driven by the growing interest in learning more about China and its culture. FRANKFURT, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- At the Frankfurt Book Fair, books are more than products on display. For many international readers and publishing professionals, they offer a window into China, its history, culture, society and changing ways of life. This year, about 170 Chinese publishing institutions are taking part in the five-day fair, with up to 55 events ranging from discussions and rights negotiations to signing ceremonies and new book launches. Through books, translations and face-to-face exchanges, Chinese publishers are seeking to bring more stories about China to global audiences while deepening ties with their international counterparts. The presence of Chinese publishers at the world's largest book fair is driven by the growing interest in learning more about China and its culture. Speaking for readers in his country, Mohamad El Khatib, CEO of Digital Future, a Lebanese publishing house, told Xinhua that China is becoming more famous in many countries, especially in Arab countries. Chinese stories resonate with readers in Arab countries because they "share a lot of values", Khatib noted. "That makes us look a lot into values and talk about Chinese culture-its values, how it respects families, how it respects life, parents and all of these things." Christina Werum-Wang, German director of the Frankfurt Confucius Institute, believes that book is one of the best ways for people to understand China if they do not have a Chinese friend. She made the remarks at an event named "Curated Classics: Chinese Masterpieces" organized by China International Book Trading Corporation (CIBTC). This event brings together several distinguished Chinese publishing houses, each presenting its latest flagship title. From literary fiction to scholarly works, the selected books represent some of the best of contemporary Chinese publishing, offering international rights professionals a curated window into China's vibrant literary landscape. Literature is the true mergence of language and culture, the expression and reflection of culture by means of language, Werum-Wang explained and added that European readers have gained yet another gateway to discover excellent Chinese books through the "Literary Selection" initiative. The exhibits at the shared booth of the Chinese publishers at the Frankfurt Book Fair go far beyond books. At a corner of the booth, lines of panda plush toys are displayed on racks, attracting swarms of curious visitors among whom Alexander B. Voegele looked pleased to receive one panda plush toy as a gift. As a Berlin resident, Voegele is no stranger to the panda mania as pandas in the Zoo Berlin are among the most popular animals. For Voegele, the panda is a "very likable animal" that doesn't need to speak. "It wins people's hearts." Voegele is giving the panda plush toy to his niece's daughter. "She's getting it so she can start developing a feeling for China." Beyond physical cultural symbols like pandas, digital publishing products showcased by gaming enterprises such as HoYoverse have also drawn substantial crowds to the China booth. A HoYoverse insider noted that video games serve as a novel cultural entry point. Players are often drawn to traditional cultural motifs within gameplay, which subsequently inspires them to read books, appreciate traditional performances, and explore authentic cultural roots offline. Creating this seamless trajectory from virtual gameplay to multidimensional cultural experiences is precisely what the company hopes to achieve.■

item.title: Xinjiang scientific expedition finds "most resilient desert plant"
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
URUMQI, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- A type of moss discovered in a desert in northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region can survive conditions that would kill most plants, including severe dehydration, intense radiation, extreme cold and Mars-like space environments. This finding is among the major advances of the Third Xinjiang Scientific Expedition, which were released on Saturday in Urumqi, the regional capital city. Scientists describe the moss, Syntrichia caninervis, as "the most resilient desert plant found to date." The latest evidence of its remarkable resilience was uncovered in space. In March this year, the dried moss was carried aboard China's test cargo spacecraft Qingzhou for an orbital life-restart experiment. Facing microgravity and cosmic radiation, a controlled watering system gave the plants only a tiny amount of liquid water. Yet, the dried moss revived, changing from gray-black to yellow-green. "This is the first case in which a complete plant has been brought into low Earth orbit and successfully revived," said Li Xiaoshuang, a researcher at the Xinjiang Institute of Ecology and Geography under the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Continued in-orbit observation found the moss regenerating and thriving, indicating that it is an ideal material for deep-space life science research, Li added. In 2024, Li, as the first author, published the moss study in an academic journal, The Innovation, saying it is a promising pioneer plant for "colonizing extraterrestrial environments." Before the space test, scientists had already determined its genetic potential on Earth. Researchers of the Xinjiang scientific expedition discovered the plant in the Gurbantunggut Desert. After lab analysis, researchers found that the plant could tolerate the dehydration of more than 98 percent of its cells, survive rapid freezing at minus 196 degrees Celsius, and overcome strong gamma radiation. To understand how it endures such extremes, researchers obtained high-quality chromosome-level genetic information and found a large number of stress-related genes, unraveling the molecular code underlying this species' tolerance to extreme conditions. It can provide genetic material for improving crops and restoring desertified land, Li said. The Third Xinjiang Scientific Expedition was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Science and Technology. The previous two were conducted in the 1950s and 1980s, respectively. Over the past five years, the expedition team carried out studies on Xinjiang's ecology, land and agriculture, biodiversity and biological resources, mineral, energy and water resources. ■

item.title: Descendants of Doolittle Raid participants visit Shangrao, China's Jiangxi
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
A descendant of a rescued Doolittle Raid participant (R) hugs a descendant of a Chinese villager who took part in the rescue in Shangrao, east China's Jiangxi Province, Oct. 10, 2026. The Doolittle Raid, planned and led by U.S. Lieutenant Colonel James Doolittle on April 18, 1942, was an air raid on Japan as a retaliation for the attack on the U.S. Pearl Harbor. After the raid, 15 planes heading for an airport in Quzhou ran out of fuel and crashed in various localities in east China. Chinese villagers risked their lives to rescue the parachuting airmen and helped them evacuate to safety. Of the 75 airmen aboard the planes, 64 were rescued by the Chinese people. However, many locals were suspected of sheltering the Americans, and some were tortured or even killed by Japanese soldiers. In China, the Doolittle story has long been regarded as a symbol of the friendship forged between the Chinese and American peoples during their joint fight against fascism. On Oct. 10, 6 representatives of descendants of the Doolittle Raid participants visited Shangrao to view a historical exhibition, revisit rescue sites and pay tribute to the Chinese people who rescued American airmen 84 years ago. item.title: Documentary | Iowa, Across the Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
Are China and the United States partners, or adversaries? Can people-to-people exchanges reduce misunderstanding and the risk of miscalculation in one of the world's most consequential bilateral relationships? In this documentary, Xinhua's Miao Xiaojuan meets several of President Xi Jinping's longtime Iowan friends, retraces the 1985 visit that shaped his first impressions of America, and follows young Iowans now crossing the Pacific in the other direction to see China for themselves. Their stories reveal a more personal, everyday side of a world leader, and a relationship still being written by a new generation. A Miao Xiaojuan Studio Film A Xinhua News Agency Production

item.title: Taiwan leader's speech exposes him as threat to peace: mainland defense spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
BEIJING, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te's recent speech has once again exposed his true colors as a source of trouble for Taiwan and a threat to peace, said a Chinese defense spokesperson on Sunday. Chen Xi, a spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense, made the remarks when asked to comment on the speech delivered by Lai in Taiwan on Saturday, in which the Taiwan leader reiterated his secessionist agenda and stoked cross-Strait tensions. Chen noted that in recent years, the Democratic Progressive Party authorities have pursued separatism and rejected reunification for their own party interests, undermining stability in the Taiwan Strait and sacrificing the island's future. The Chinese People's Liberation Army's regular drills and training activities around the island are carried out to deter separatist activities seeking "Taiwan independence" and plots of external interference, and to safeguard the security and well-being of Taiwan compatriots, the spokesperson said. "We hope Taiwan compatriots will join the mainland in combating separatist forces, opposing external interference, safeguarding peace, and sharing the fruits of national rejuvenation," Chen added. The Taiwan question originated from a civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, while the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. ■

item.title: China's trade strength rooted in competitiveness, not currency depreciation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- China has reaffirmed its stance on its foreign exchange policy amid increased discussions over the yuan's valuation, as solid facts and figures support the view that the country's export strength is rooted in its industrial competitiveness rather than currency valuation. China has neither the need nor the intention to gain trade advantages through currency devaluation, the People's Bank of China (PBOC) said in a policy statement released on Thursday, stressing that the country has never resorted to competitive devaluation. The statement came as some countries pointed to currency valuation as a cause of trade imbalances, thereby oversimplifying the dynamics between exchange rates and trade. The conventional view that currency appreciation weakens export competitiveness largely reflects a short-term and static perspective. Over a longer horizon, competitiveness is shaped by much more than exchange rates, analysts have said. This is particularly evident in China's case. The international competitiveness of Chinese products has at times continued to strengthen even as the RMB appreciated. From 2020 to 2021, the RMB appreciated by about 9 percent against the U.S. dollar, while China's share of global exports increased by 1.7 percentage points in this period, according to the PBOC. In 2022, by contrast, the RMB depreciated by more than 8 percent against the dollar, while China's share of global exports fell by 0.7 percentage points, PBOC said. These figures showed that China's imports and exports are relatively insensitive to exchange-rate movements, while neither its goods trade surplus nor its current-account surplus has a simple linear relationship with the RMB exchange rate, said Guan Tao, chief economist at Huafu Securities Co., Ltd. Attributing China's export strength primarily to currency depreciation or other purported factors including "overcapacity" reflects a fundamental misunderstanding of the sophistication and competitiveness of the country's industrial sector. At its core, China's trade growth is underpinned by its vast domestic market, comprehensive industrial and supply chains, well-developed infrastructure, abundant and highly skilled workforce, and steadily improving research and innovation capabilities, the central bank noted. Dong Ximiao, chief economist at China Merchants Union Consumer Finance, said that historically, the world's major trade surplus countries have generally been those with strong industrial competitiveness. For deficit economies, their deeper challenges lie in structural factors such as low savings rates, high consumption and insufficient industrial competitiveness, issues that cannot be resolved simply by focusing on the exchange rates of their trading partners. "Declining trade competitiveness in some countries reflects their own structural difficulties," said Hao Yubiao, director of the National Center for Economic Security Studies at Capital University of Economics and Business. "Pointing the finger at other countries' currency exchange rates amounts to avoiding the need for domestic adjustment and does little to solve the underlying problems." At a time when currencies in neighboring countries have been depreciating, China has refrained from pursuing beggar-thy-neighbor policies or competitive devaluation. This year, both the onshore and offshore RMB have strengthened past the 6.7 mark against the U.S. dollar. China had never resorted to competitive currency devaluation to boost exports to offset intensive external shocks in the past, the central bank said. Over the past two decades, the RMB has experienced multiple cycles of appreciation and depreciation, reflecting increasingly pronounced two-way movements and greater exchange-rate flexibility. The PBOC said that looking ahead, both appreciation and depreciation factors remain in play and that the future direction of the RMB exchange rates remains uncertain. Such two-way fluctuations are consistent with China's efforts to make the exchange rate more flexible and market-oriented. As a responsible major economy, China has also been committed to addressing such trade imbalances via international cooperation. At a meeting of G20 finance ministers and central bank governors last month, PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng said structural reforms are needed across economies to address global trade imbalances. He called on deficit economies to reduce fiscal deficits and raise domestic savings rates, while surplus economies should appropriately promote growth in consumption and investment. Countries should formulate medium- and long-term policy plans, make clear commitments and follow through on those commitments, Pan said. ■

item.title: Thriving exchanges add new momentum to China-Botswana partnership
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11
by Xinhua writer Guo Chunju GABORONE, Oct. 11 (Xinhua) -- Botswanan President Duma Gideon Boko will pay a state visit to China from Oct. 12 to 17 at the invitation of Chinese President Xi Jinping, as the two countries seek to deepen cooperation in trade, investment and people-to-people exchanges. In January 2025, Xi and Boko exchanged congratulations on the 50th anniversary of diplomatic ties, expressing confidence in the prospects for closer cooperation. In September 2024, the two countries elevated their bilateral ties to a strategic partnership. Beyond these diplomatic milestones, cooperation between both countries has taken shape in projects ranging from energy and mining to education and health care. IMPROVING LOCAL LIVELIHOODS Chinese-invested companies have maintained steady cooperation with Botswana for years, covering areas such as infrastructure, energy and mining, bringing tangible benefits to local communities. Water infrastructure projects have helped improve access to essential services across Botswana. The Thune Dam, constructed by Chinese companies, supplies water for domestic and agricultural use, with its water resources integrated into Botswana's North-South Water Carrier system. Other projects, including water supply and sanitation works in Maun and the Boteti region, are also helping improve local water services. Meanwhile, the Digital Delta Data Center is strengthening Botswana's digital infrastructure and supporting the growth of its digital economy. Cooperation in energy and mining is creating further opportunities for development. The Jwaneng 100 MW Solar Power Plant project has officially commenced operations, helping to ease Botswana's electricity shortage and strengthen the country's energy security. Meanwhile, the Khoemacau Copper Mine Expansion Project is expected to boost production and generate employment opportunities. The establishment of the Mining Centre of Excellence at Maun Technical College with the support of Botswana's Ministry of Higher Education also helps equip young people with practical skills tailored to the needs of the mining industry, linking vocational training more closely with local employment. Beyond economic development, cooperation has also extended to healthcare and education. The teaching hospital at the University of Botswana School of Medicine in Gaborone supports medical care and training, while four China-aided primary schools have improved learning conditions for local children, contributing to the development of Botswana's basic education system. EXPANDING TRADE, DEEPENING COOPERATION Economic and trade cooperation between China and Botswana is mutually beneficial and enjoys broad prospects. Bilateral business trips and engagements have become increasingly frequent, with continued exchange between the two sides. From May 1 this year, China extended zero-tariff treatment to all 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic ties, bringing significant benefits to Botswana's premium products, such as beef and citrus. "This important initiative opens new opportunities for Botswana to expand its exports, strengthen trade and deepen our economic cooperation with China," said Botswana's Minister for State President, Defense and Security Moeti Mohwasa. Two-way trade between China and Botswana reached 1.222 billion U.S. dollars in 2025, an increase of 21.3 percent year on year, and rose by 58.6 percent to 852 million U.S. dollars in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period last year, official statistics showed. In January 2021, the two countries signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for cooperation on the Belt and Road Initiative, making Botswana the 46th African partner country to join the initiative. In 2025, the two countries signed a MoU on promoting the implementation of the Global Development Initiative, and Botswana joined the Initiative on International Trade and Economic Cooperation Framework for Digital Economy and Green Development. These bilateral agreements provide new opportunities, expand cooperation into new sectors, and open up new prospects for China-Botswana practical cooperation. Many Chinese business delegations have visited Botswana to explore market opportunities, while Botswana's officials and think tank representatives have praised the achievements of Chinese modernization following visits to China. Viewing China as "a constant friend and a reliable development partner," Botswana seeks to learn from China's achievements in improving people's living standards and poverty alleviation, as the southern African country pursues its own development agenda, seeking investment, partnerships, and alignment between development strategies. BRINGING PEOPLE CLOSER People-to-people exchanges have brought the two peoples closer through cultural, educational and community activities, including "Chinese Bridge" competitions, film festivals and medical outreach programs by Chinese medical teams. The Confucius Institutes at the University of Botswana in Gaborone and the Botswana International University of Science and Technology (BIUST) in Palapye in central Botswana run programs on promoting Chinese language education and cultural exchange. "By learning the Chinese language, our students gain a key to unlocking opportunities in a rapidly globalizing world," said BIUST Vice Chancellor Otlogetswe Totolo, describing the institute as a platform for cultural exchange, academic collaboration and closer friendship between Botswana and China. The growing popularity of the Chinese language and culture among the people of Botswana has helped strengthen people-to-people ties and deepen bilateral friendship, while more Botswana people are looking forward to opportunities to visit China. "The relationship between Botswana and China has grown steadily over many decades, bringing cooperation for many, many years of mutual interests," said Botswana's Minister of International Relations Phenyo Butale. Over the years, bilateral partnership in the health sector has continued to flourish. Since 1981, 18 successive groups of Chinese medical professionals, comprising more than 600 experts in total, have traveled thousands of miles to serve in Botswana. They have become an integral part of Botswana's healthcare system, providing specialized medical care to local communities and strengthening bilateral cooperation. "Their dedication has significantly improved access to specialized healthcare, enhanced the quality of medical services, strengthened the capacity of our healthcare system, and ultimately contributed to improving the health outcomes of our people," said Tshepo Machacha, acting permanent secretary of Botswana's Ministry of Health. Machacha himself has received traditional Chinese acupuncture therapy. He said traditional Chinese medicine has enriched Botswana's healthcare system. "This serves as a practical demonstration of how cultural exchange and medical cooperation can directly improve patient care while strengthening medical understanding between the two nations," he said.■

item.title: China, EU reaffirm stable, balanced ties as key trading partners: commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- China and the European Union (EU) have reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining stable and balanced trade ties as key trading partners after a meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism, an official with China's commerce ministry said Saturday. Chinese Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao and European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maros Sefcovic jointly chaired the second meeting of the consultation mechanism from Thursday to Friday in Beijing. The two sides confirmed that they would address trade and economic differences and each other's concerns in a balanced manner within the framework of World Trade Organization (WTO) rules, explore ways to deepen mutually beneficial cooperation, and promote balanced growth and further development in China-EU trade. Both sides agreed the consultation mechanism had been operating smoothly and efficiently, and that "the successful convening of its second meeting marked a new beginning rather than an end," said the official. The outcomes agreed upon at the meeting demonstrated that China and the EU had both the willingness and the wisdom to manage and properly resolve differences through dialogue and consultation, effectively preventing tensions from escalating, the official said. The two sides held intensive consultations in a spirit of mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit, discussing in depth ways to address each other's concerns on an equal footing, expand two-way market access and promote dynamic balance in China-EU trade, covering topics including medical devices, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, inverters, and agri-food products. According to the official, the two sides agreed to explore the possibility of reducing tariffs on certain goods within the framework of WTO rules, and hold a technical dialogue on the EU's Foreign Subsidies Regulation. In-depth discussions were also held on trade in electric and hybrid vehicles, which helped prevent further escalation, effectively safeguarded the actual export interests of Chinese companies and supported the stable development of China-EU trade in hybrid vehicles. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to addressing each other's concerns regarding export controls. The EU side will continue to work toward making progress in resolving key licensing cases involving China in the dual-use sector, said the official. They agreed that China and the EU have significant potential for cooperation in new energy, artificial intelligence, trade in services, the digital economy, and green and low-carbon development, and that they could further explore new opportunities and expand areas of cooperation. China will continue to welcome EU companies investing and doing business in China and to improve its business environment, said the official. China also expects the EU to provide Chinese companies with a fair, transparent and predictable business environment, effectively protect their legitimate rights and interests, and strengthen their confidence and expectations regarding investment and business operations in the EU. Looking ahead, the two sides will step up efforts on key trade and economic issues of mutual concern and work together to implement the outcomes and agreements reached at the meeting, said the official. They also agreed to hold the third meeting of the mechanism in March 2027. In the meantime, they will maintain close communication at all levels, including through a ministerial-level video conference next January. It was agreed that stable and healthy China-EU economic and trade relations serve their shared interests and also inject certainty and positive momentum into global economic growth and the stability of industrial and supply chains, said the official. ■

item.title: 90 years on, Long March spirit endures in China, resonates beyond borders
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10
*The Long March spirit highlights the firm faith, strong will, and never-give-up attitude of the whole Party and all Chinese people to overcome major challenges during the revolutionary years. *In today's environment, people need to hold fast to the same values that made the Long March an epic undertaking in modern Chinese history, said Khairy Tourk, professor of economics at the Stuart School of Business at the Illinois Institute of Technology in Chicago. *The Long March is not only a towering monument in the development of the Chinese nation, but also a precious spiritual asset for all humanity in the pursuit of independence, freedom and liberation, said Etienne Bankuwiha, a Burundian sinologist. BEIJING, Oct. 10 (Xinhua) -- This year marks the 105th founding anniversary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. The arduous journey, which lasted from 1934 to 1936, helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. Nearly a century later, the Long March remains an important window into China's history and development. "The Long March is like a spine of your body that goes right through the modern history of China," said Harold Weldon, an Australian publisher and filmmaker. For China watchers, understanding this pivotal chapter is essential to understanding the CPC's founding ideals and enduring mission, as well as the resilient spirit of the Chinese nation. GREAT TURNING POINT The victory of the Long March marked a great turning point for the CPC and the Chinese revolution, and stands as a towering monument in the historic process of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. During the epic military trek, the CPC-led Red Army broke through encirclement by Kuomintang forces. Red Army soldiers braved raging rivers, snow-covered mountains and treacherous grasslands, with some marching as far as 12,500 kilometers. "It was probably the greatest tale of human endurance in recorded history, I think, in terms of the hardships faced," said Weldon. The Long March is a classic example of the ability of the Chinese people to defy overwhelming odds, and is ready to put up with huge sacrifices in treasure and blood in order to achieve their goals, said Khairy Tourk, professor of economics at the Stuart School of Business at the Illinois Institute of Technology in Chicago, noting that "sacrifice is an essential part of achieving glorious victories." Paul Ilado, editorial director of Kenya's Radio Africa Group, said the Long March transformed a military retreat into a decisive political and historical turning point. The Red Army was under enormous pressure, he noted, and their ability to survive the encirclement campaign was crucial to the continuation of the movement. The historical significance of the Long March extends beyond military survival, Ilado said. As part of the CPC's revolutional legacy, he said, the Long March demonstrated that hardship had to be overcome, objectives pursued over the long term, and survival under extreme pressure sustained by organization and discipline. During the Long March, Red Army officers and soldiers were pushed to the extremes of their physical limits, turning this dramatic episode in world military history into a "glorious human miracle." The Long March spirit highlights the firm faith, strong will, and never-give-up attitude of the whole Party and all Chinese people to overcome major challenges during the revolutionary years. Wagner Lacerda Dantas, a Brazilian journalist with China International Communications Group, described the spirit as the determination to continue fighting for a collective goal even when circumstances appear almost impossible, bringing together conviction, courage, discipline, solidarity, sacrifice and confidence in victory. "What impressed me the most was the organizational cohesion and belief of the Red Army, although under extremely tough conditions," said Balew Demissie, senior consultant at the Policy Studies Institute of Ethiopia. When facing extreme natural environments such as snow-capped mountains and marshlands, as well as the chasing and interception by the enemy's materially superior forces, this army did not collapse, but instead demonstrated astonishing discipline and idealism, and ultimately achieved success, he added. Yuri Tavrovsky, head of the Expert Council of the Russian-Chinese Committee for Friendship, Peace and Development, likewise identifies endurance, sacrifice, patriotism and wisdom as qualities forged during the Long March. In his view, the experience helped shape a generation of leaders capable of confronting crises, assessing changing circumstances and finding a way forward. CONTEMPORARY ECHO The Long March belongs to a specific historical period, and China's circumstances today are vastly different from those of the 1930s, but foreign observers see its enduring relevance in the CPC's strong leadership and China's rapid development. In today's environment, people need to hold fast to the same values that made the Long March an epic undertaking in modern Chinese history, said Tourk, the economics professor at the Illinois Institute of Technology. "Without values such as sacrifice, patriotism, perseverance, and firmness, the people would lose their sense of direction," he said. "I believe that understanding the Long March is truly one of the best ways to understand how the Communist Party of China managed to grow under such adverse circumstances," said Dantas, the Brazilian journalist, adding that it demonstrated characteristics such as discipline, unity, organizational capacity, independence and autonomy, seeking truth from facts, and, above all, confidence in the masses. "The great strength of the Party during that period lay not only in its weapons, but in its ability to maintain close ties with the people," he said. Etienne Bankuwiha, a Burundian sinologist, said that amid life-and-death trials, Chinese Communists demonstrated unshakable ideals and convictions and made strategic choices decisive for the future of the Chinese revolution. "For China today, it remains a powerful source of motivation that encourages the people to overcome difficulties, advance Chinese modernization, and realize the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation," he added. During a visit to China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, Ilado, the editorial director of Kenya's Radio Africa Group, was struck by the transformation of land that had once been difficult to cultivate, which offered him a tangible way to think about the legacy of the Long March. "When I arrived in China and went to Ningxia, I was amazed at how a desert had been turned into productive land, and how today that area has become a breadbasket for the country and the world," he said. The connection, Ilado stressed, is the idea of undertaking a difficult journey over a long period without losing sight of the destination. A farmer cultivating difficult land, an engineer building irrigation infrastructure, a technician improving food processing or a young person leaving a poor rural community to pursue education may seem far removed from the Red Army of the 1930s, yet all can be understood through the determination to continue when the destination is still far away, Ilado noted. Joshua Kingdom, a research fellow at Uganda's Development Watch Center, sees the Long March spirit reflected in China's response to contemporary challenges. He said China's efforts to withstand external pressure demonstrated resilience and a determination to deepen cooperation with Global South economies rather than succumb to difficulties. BEYOND CHINA The significance of the Long March extends beyond the history of China. The Long March spirit of unwavering faith, perseverance and collective spirit transcends borders and ideologies, inspiring humanity to overcome adversity and strive for a brighter future. Demissie, the senior consultant at Ethiopia's Policy Studies Institute, said the success of the Long March contributed directly to the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. In his view, the independent and modern state that emerged from that history has since become an important force in promoting multipolarity, South-South cooperation and the rise of the Global South. The Long March is not only a towering monument in the development of the Chinese nation, but also a precious spiritual asset for all humanity in the pursuit of independence, freedom and liberation, said Etienne, the Burundian sinologist. "Seen from the broader perspective of the Global South, the Long March proves a compelling point: to achieve genuine liberation and prosperity, a country and its people must proceed from their own conditions, uphold independence and self-reliance, and defeat every obstacle through unity and struggle," he said. Dennis Munene, executive director of the China-Africa Center at the Africa Policy Institute, said the Long March spirit could encourage the international community to unite around common goals and pursue dialogue across civilizations to address conflicts, climate change and poverty. These challenges cannot be resolved overnight; they require sustained commitment, cooperation and a willingness to keep working despite setbacks, he added. Kingdom, the research fellow at Uganda's Development Watch Center, said that writings by people like Edgar Snow about the Long March have moved people across the globe, "because every individual, wherever they are living, they usually have fears to conquer." "So, I feel like when you have examples of people who have gone the extra mile to conquer different things that are really relatable in some sense, it moves people," he said.
